name: stmr.c
reason: Opened the repo page and readme.md: a plain port of Martin Porter's stemming algorithm as a C library plus CLI (MIT, 44 stars). No benchmark, speed claim or comparison with any other stemmer anywhere in the readme or file list (stmr.c, stmr.h, test.c, fixture/); test.c only checks correctness against fixtures.

name: str
listed_description: Yet another string library for C language.
reason: Opened the repo page, README.md, api.md, changes-from-v1.md and the v1 branch README: no benchmark, no speed claim and no bench directory (file list: src, test-data, str.h, api.md, Makefile). Only design remark is that a str is a pointer plus a byte count so it is cheap to pass by value. BSD-3-Clause, 363 stars, last commit 2026-01-02.

name: talloc
listed_description: Hierarchical, reference-counted memory pool system with destructors.
reason: talloc.samba.org is EGRESS_BLOCKED. Read the Samba GitHub mirror (samba-team/samba lib/talloc): testsuite.c has test_speed (talloc vs malloc, talloc_pool vs malloc, talloc_zero vs calloc, ops/sec over 5 s) but no committed results; talloc.h says talloc_pool exists because malloc was a large CPU consumer in Samba 3.2 profiling, with no numbers. A search snippet attributes to the talloc docs 'about 4% slower than malloc on an x86 Debian box' (page not opened, and it is a slowdown). ccan tal benchmark speed.c (tal vs talloc vs malloc) also has no committed results. No number showing talloc beating a baseline reachable. Lead: Samba git commit messages for talloc_pool may carry timings; not reachable here.

name: tinyexpr
listed_description: Tiny recursive-descent parser, compiler and evaluation engine for simple mathematical expressions.
reason: Own benchmark.c table in the README compares te_eval to natively compiled C and every row is slower: sqrt(a^1.5+a^2.5) 15,641 ms vs 14,478 ms (8% slower), a+5 765 vs 563 ms (36% slower), (a+5)*2 1422 vs 563 ms (153% slower), (1/(a+1)+2/(a+2)+3/(a+3)) 5,516 vs 1,266 ms (336% slower). The prose says 'pretty fast compared to C' only for short or pow-heavy expressions, not backed by a faster row. Independent newlawrence/Parsers-Benchmark README example puts TinyExpr (168.341 ns) tenth of ten parsers (ATMSP, ExprTk, FParser, Lepton, MathExpr, MTParser, muParser, muParserX, TinyExpr, Calculate). Claim is small size and simplicity, not a win over any baseline; orchestrator may keep it as a not-faster documented entry from these numbers.

name: tinyheaders
listed_description: Collection of header-only libraries, primarily oriented toward game development.
reason: Repo is now RandyGaul/cute_headers (5.1k stars, zlib or public domain per header). Read the README and the headers cute_c2, cute_png, cute_sound, cute_net, cute_spritebatch, cute_tiled, cute_aseprite, cute_sync, cute_tls, and the issues search for 'benchmark' (one unrelated issue, cute_alloc alignment #105): no benchmark against any baseline. Only numeric statement is the cute_png 1.06 changelog '50-75x better compression for typical images', which compares its own new LZ77 writer to its old RLE writer on ratio, not speed. cute_c2 says boolean tests are faster than manifold tests (internal comparison, no numbers).

name: tlsf
listed_description: Two-Level Segregated Fit allocator; a general-purpose, dynamic memory allocator specifically designed to meet real-time requirements.
reason: Original site www.gii.upv.es and the ECRTS 2004 paper (Masmano, Ripoll, Crespo, Real), the York 2008 paper page, embedded.com, TU Dresden slides, lore.barebox.org and lists.infradead.org are all EGRESS_BLOCKED. Reachable TLSF code (mattconte/tlsf, rmind/tlsf, sysprog21/tlsf-bsd README and docs) has no baseline numbers; tlsf-bsd docs give a 42 ns median WCET with no comparison. Independent r-lyeh-archived/malloc-survey (MSVC 190023419 release, 2016) shows tlsf::allocator 157187 us vs std::allocator 117766 us, 1.33x slower; its faster 'dumb_tlsf' is a simplified variant. Search snippets say dlmalloc is faster on average and TLSF targets worst-case time; paper numbers not seen. Leads: paper-access retier (ECRTS 2004 tables vs Doug Lea malloc); yvt/rlsf (Rust TLSF, STM32F401 260-320 cycles vs dlmalloc 450-750) and XenoAtom.Allocators (C# TLSF) are already in the wave 11 catalog; SakshamSaharia/tlsf_allocator README claims about 5% faster than malloc/free over 10 million ops (student implementation, no flags or CPU).
